happy
開心
What small event could make an ordinary day feel happy for you?
A short call from an old friend would make me happy. Remembering that someone thought of me can change the whole afternoon.
老朋友突然打來聊幾句，就能讓我開心。知道有人想到我，整個下午都會不一樣。
sad
難過
How would you respond to a friend who feels sad but does not want advice?
I would let my friend be sad without trying to fix everything. Sitting together quietly could be more helpful than offering solutions.
我會讓朋友安心難過，不急著把一切解決。安靜陪著，可能比一直提辦法更有幫助。
angry
生氣
What would you do before replying to a message that made you angry?
I would wait until I felt less angry before replying. Reading the message again might help me separate the facts from my first reaction.
我會等沒那麼生氣再回覆。重讀一次，也許能分清楚實際內容和自己的第一反應。
afraid
害怕
How could you try something unfamiliar even when you feel afraid?
If I felt afraid, I would start with a small, safe step. Knowing I could stop would make the attempt less intimidating.
害怕時，我會先試一個小而安全的步驟。知道自己隨時能停，就比較敢嘗試。
anxious
焦慮
Waiting for an important result makes you anxious. What could you do while waiting?
When I am anxious, I give myself a specific time to check for news. Between checks, a practical task helps occupy my attention.
焦慮的時候，我會訂好查看消息的時間。其他時候做點實際的事，讓注意力有地方放。
nervous
緊張
What would help you feel less nervous before meeting a new group?
I would prepare a simple introduction when I felt nervous. Arriving a little early would let me meet people one at a time.
緊張時，我會先準備簡單的自我介紹。早到一點，就能慢慢認識人，不必一下子面對整群。
excited
興奮
How would you share exciting news without overwhelming the person listening?
I would say why I was excited and pause for their response. They might want to ask questions before hearing every detail.
我會先說自己為什麼興奮，再停一下聽對方回應。他可能想先問問題，不是立刻聽完所有細節。
disappointed
失望
You are disappointed after an event is cancelled. How would you handle the evening?
I would admit I was disappointed rather than pretend it did not matter. Then I would choose a smaller activity I could still enjoy.
我會承認自己失望，不假裝沒關係。再找一件今晚仍然能享受的小活動。
frustrate
挫折
What can frustrate you when you are learning a new skill?
Unclear instructions can frustrate me more than a difficult task. Seeing one complete example usually helps me find a starting point.
比起任務難，說明不清楚更讓我挫折。看過一個完整例子，通常就比較知道怎麼開始。
embarrassed
尷尬
You feel embarrassed after forgetting someone's name. What would you say?
I would admit I felt embarrassed and ask for the name again. A sincere question is better than avoiding the person all evening.
我會坦白說有點尷尬，請對方再說一次名字。真誠地問，總比整晚躲著他好。
proud
自豪
What achievement could make you proud even if nobody else noticed it?
I would feel proud of finishing a difficult personal project. Knowing I kept going would matter even without public recognition.
完成困難的個人計畫，就值得自豪。就算沒人注意，自己知道有堅持下去也很重要。
hopeful
希望
What makes you feel hopeful after a setback?
I feel hopeful when I can identify one useful next step. A clear action makes the situation feel less fixed.
看見下一個能做的步驟，我就比較有希望。有具體行動，就不覺得事情已經完全定局。
calm
冷靜
How would you stay calm while helping someone who is upset?
I would stay calm by slowing my speech and listening first. Matching their frustration would probably make the conversation harder.
我會放慢說話速度，先聽對方說，讓自己保持冷靜。跟著激動起來，事情只會更難談。
content
滿足
What helps you feel content without comparing your life with others?
I feel content when I notice what is already working in my day. A peaceful meal and an honest conversation can be enough.
注意到生活裡已經不錯的部分，就比較滿足。安心吃頓飯、真誠聊個天，也能很美好。
jealous
羨慕
How could you respond constructively when you feel jealous of a friend's success?
I would notice what made me jealous and what it revealed about my goals. I could congratulate my friend while working on my own direction.
我會想想自己羨慕的是什麼，看看那是不是自己的目標。祝福朋友，也繼續走自己的路。
surprise
驚喜
What kind of surprise would you enjoy, and what kind would make you uncomfortable?
I would enjoy a small surprise meal with close friends. An unexpected party with a large crowd might feel overwhelming instead.
和好友吃一頓驚喜晚餐，我會很開心。突然來一大群人的派對，反而可能讓我不自在。
regret
後悔
How can regret become useful rather than keep you stuck?
Regret becomes useful when it helps me change a future action. I can apologize or prepare differently instead of replaying the same moment.
後悔如果能讓下次做法不同，就有意義。我可以道歉、換個準備方式，不只是一直重想那一刻。
cope
應付
How would you cope when several small problems arrived at once?
I would cope by separating urgent tasks from things that could wait. Asking for one specific piece of help would make the load smaller.
我會先分出急事和能等的事，再慢慢應付。請人協助其中一件，也能減輕負擔。
mood
心情
How might you explain a quiet mood without making a friend feel unwelcome?
I would explain that my mood was quiet, not unfriendly. I could suggest a relaxed activity that did not require much conversation.
我會說明今天心情比較安靜，不是拒絕對方。可以一起做點輕鬆、不用一直說話的事。
emotion
情緒
Why might naming an emotion help during a difficult conversation?
Naming the emotion could make my reaction easier to explain. Saying I feel hurt is clearer than expecting someone to guess.
說出情緒，能讓我的反應比較容易說明。直接說自己受傷了，比讓對方去猜更清楚。
feeling
感覺
A friend has a different feeling about a shared experience. How would you respond?
I would ask what created that feeling for them. Sharing an event does not mean we noticed or needed the same things.
我會問，是什麼讓他有那種感覺。一起經歷事情，不代表注意到的和需要的都一樣。
overwhelm
壓垮
What could stop a long list of responsibilities from beginning to overwhelm you?
A huge list can overwhelm me if every task looks equally urgent. I would choose one next action and set the rest aside temporarily.
一長串事情看起來都很急時，很容易把我壓垮。我會先選下一步，其餘暫時放旁邊。
comfort
安慰
What would bring comfort to someone who has had a difficult week?
A familiar meal might bring comfort without requiring a long explanation. I would ask whether they wanted company or some time alone.
一頓熟悉的飯菜，也許就能帶來安慰，不必解釋太多。我會問他想有人陪，還是想獨處。
optimistic
樂觀
How can you remain optimistic without ignoring a genuine problem?
I can be optimistic about making progress while acknowledging the problem. A realistic backup plan does not cancel my hope that things will improve.
我可以對進展保持樂觀，也承認問題存在。準備實際的備案，不代表放棄改善的希望。
